findings.claim: The generated summary and evaluator both omit the consequential exception boundary around filters and listeners.
evidence: @investigram-f0c3a29d explains awaited invocation and the result/error filters, but does not explain that successful-value classification and notification are inside the broad try/catch.
@investigram-8437cd7c delegates dispatch to Event without stating that listener exceptions can affect execution.
Evaluator answers 1 and 2 repeat the normal classification account and list runtime/dispatch unknowns but do not identify this specific exception-boundary limitation.
Frozen reference material limits explicitly state that filter and listener exceptions can affect execution and that the broad try/catch encloses successful-value classification and notification.
findings.consequence: The summary can leave a reader with an incomplete model of what may enter error classification or disrupt an invocation, particularly when supplying custom filters or listeners.
findings.uncertainty: Neither the view nor evaluator explicitly claims that only fn exceptions are handled or that all callbacks are safe. This is an omitted qualification, not a demonstrated evaluator assertion of those stronger false claims. The reference supplies no runtime test or exhaustive callback outcome analysis.

subjectUsefulness.judgment: Useful as a qualified overview of an invocation, classification, and observation boundary and as a starting point for focused investigation; incomplete for reasoning about callback exception behavior and cumbersome to scan.
reasons: The frozen reference supports the central responsibility assignment, tag distinctions, conditional timing, fresh listener state on clone, value-failure unwrapping, and external ownership of retry loops.
The evaluator successfully preserves interpretation status and distinguishes summary composition from later investigation and correction history.
Individually identified component accounts give a concrete follow-up target, and the evaluator correctly treats its proposed lens as a future request.
The evaluator identifies visible repetition and peripheral reporting that compete with the functional explanation.
limitations: Filter/listener exception effects and the breadth of the try/catch are materially absent from the generated account and evaluator understanding.
The frozen reference cannot independently settle several displayed defaults, clock details, and consumer-specific claims; these are not demonstrated generation errors or evaluator extrapolations.
Only a summary is supplied, so progressive clarification, actual correction/reconsideration behavior, and navigation usability cannot be assessed.
No runtime test was performed, and caller operations and filters may perform arbitrary work.
The reference preparer and orchestrator are the implementing agent, with an unavailable exact model identifier in the OpenAI family; this overlap limits assessment independence.
